Over the past three months, headline inflation has risen 0.48 pp (from 2.33% to 2.81%), and the 3-month annualized pace stands at 2.33%, well above the starting point of the 12-month range. Core PCE, the Committee's preferred measure, has also accelerated, rising from 1.88% to 1.98% and now sitting essentially at the 2% target after lingering below it for most of the period shown.

The recent monthly momentum remains firm. The most recent month-on-month headline print is 0.09%, which is below the trailing 3-month average of 0.19% but comfortably above the 0.03% that was my stated falsifier threshold. The breadth of the acceleration—both headline and core moving up together—suggests this is not a transitory energy or food shock but a more persistent pressure.

Against this, the FOMC language (dated June 13, 2018) notes inflation "close to 2 percent" and expects it to remain "near" that level "over the medium term." This forward-looking framing suggests the Committee sees the recent moves as manageable. Longer-term inflation expectations are described as "little changed."

For the next month-ahead release, the momentum is still positive. While the outgoing month-on-month of 0.09% is slower than the 3-month average, it has not fallen sharply. Energy prices have not collapsed. The level of headline inflation (2.81%) and core PCE (1.98%) both point to continued upward bias near term. The risk is modest—a repeat of a sub-0.10% print or sharper energy deflation would challenge this—but the baseline remains for headline CPI to remain flat to slightly higher at the next release.

economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals.

The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals.

That view was tested against the most recent data and proved correct directionally — headline CPI rose to 2.74% y/y from the prior 2.68%, and core PCE sits at 2.81%, further above the 2% target. Core PCE sits 81 basis points above the Fed's 2% target with no imminent fade visible.

But the month-to-month acceleration has clearly stalled. The 3-month average of 0.19% m/m is down from the prior period's higher prints, and momentum has not sustained. The Fed's June statement language — "inflation remains somewhat elevated" rather than accelerating — aligns with a plateau rather than a continued push higher.

For the next monthly release, headline CPI is more likely to edge down or stay flat as the monthly pace normalizes around that 0.19% average, and base effects from last year's modest readings begin to provide gentle headwinds. A 2.65–2.75% y/y range is most probable, not a new high.
